sources.entry: Pleroma - Federated microblogging server, Mastodon, GNU social, & ActivityPub compatible. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Elixir

summary.name: Pleroma
summary.one_liner: Pleroma is a self-hostable microblogging server that federates with other ActivityPub servers such as Mastodon, Friendica, and Pixelfed.
use_cases: Host a private microblogging server for yourself or friends
Federate with Mastodon and other ActivityPub servers
Run a social server on a Raspberry Pi or low-power device
Use Mastodon-compatible client apps with a self-hosted server
Package or deploy a federated social network on Linux
summary.what_it_does: Pleroma is microblogging server software that exchanges messages with other servers implementing ActivityPub, so users can keep control of their own identity while reaching people on larger servers. It is written in Elixir and uses PostgreSQL for storage. The page says it runs efficiently on low-power devices like Raspberry Pi but scales on more powerful hardware, though only single-node for now. It supports the Mastodon client API with Pleroma extensions. Installation options named include OTP releases (recommended for Linux glibc or musl on x86/arm), building from source, OS packages, and community Docker and Raspberry Pi images.
notable: Federates with ActivityPub servers including Mastodon, Friendica, GNU Social, Hubzilla, Misskey, Peertube, and Pixelfed
Supports the Mastodon client API with Pleroma extensions
Lightweight enough for low-power devices like Raspberry Pi
Licensed AGPL-3.0 and written in Elixir with PostgreSQL
caveats: Scaling is single-node only for now, per the page
Official OTP release is for Linux (glibc or musl) on x86/arm; other platforms need building from source
The project does not provide Docker files; the page points to third-party Docker images
